_comment: IPC -> BNS starter mapping. Direction is old->new ONLY; new-code sections that have no IPC ancestor (BNS 111 organised crime, 113 terrorist act, 103(2) mob lynching, 304 snatching, 69 sexual intercourse by deceitful means) are carried as kind=new_offence rows with a null old side. Every row ships with verified_by=null and is therefore INERT: Mapping.require_verified refuses it until an operator audit signs the row off against the bare acts. new_section names the section, not the punishment sub-clause; sub-clause detail lives in notes. Schema: old_code, old_section, new_code, new_section, kind (one_to_one|changed|new_offence|deleted), verified_by, notes.

notes: Common intention. Moved out of the offences chapters into the BNS general clauses at 3(5); wording substantially retained.
Abetment of a thing.
Criminal conspiracy; definition at 61(1), punishment at 61(2).

Sedition is repealed outright. BNS 152 penalises acts endangering the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India and is NOT a like-for-like successor - the ingredients, the mens rea and the punishment all differ. Never describe 152 as 'the new 124A'.
Unlawful assembly defined at 189(1); punishment (old IPC 143) at 189(2).
Rioting; punishment at 191(2).
Promoting enmity between groups on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language.
Causing disappearance of evidence of an offence, or giving false information to screen the offender.
Rash driving or riding on a public way.
Obscene acts and songs in a public place.
Culpable homicide defined.
Murder defined, with the exceptions retained.
Punishment for murder, at 103(1). 103(2) is a NEW offence (mob lynching) carried separately in this file.
Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
Causing death by negligence. Punishment raised at 106(1) and 106(2) adds the hit-and-run offence, so this is not a pure renumbering.
Dowry death; definition and punishment retained.
Abetment of suicide.
Attempt to murder.
Attempt to commit suicide. BNS 226 is far narrower: it reaches only attempts made to compel or restrain a public servant from discharging his duty. The general offence is gone.
Assault or criminal force on a woman with intent to outrage her modesty.
Kidnapping; definition at 137(1), punishment at 137(2).
Trafficking of a person.
Rape defined.
Punishment for rape; aggravated forms sit at BNS 65-70.
Unnatural offences. Read down for consenting adults by Navtej Singh Johar (2018) and carried into no BNS section at all - the residual non-consensual conduct is prosecuted under other BNS provisions.
Theft. Punishment at 303(2), which newly allows community service for a first petty theft under five thousand rupees.
Robbery; punishment at 309(4).
Criminal breach of trust; punishment at 316(2).
Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property; punishment at 318(4).
Mischief; graded punishments at 324(2) to 324(5).
Criminal trespass and house-trespass; punishment at 329(3) and 329(4).
Forgery; punishment (old IPC 465) at 336(2).
Adultery. Struck down as unconstitutional in Joseph Shine v. Union of India (2018) and not re-enacted in the BNS.
Cruelty by a husband or his relatives; 'cruelty' is defined separately at BNS 86.
Defamation defined, at 356(1). IPC 500 maps to the same BNS section, so BNS 356 has no single IPC counterpart.
Punishment for defamation, at 356(2), which adds community service.
Criminal intimidation; punishments (old IPC 506) at 351(2) to 351(4).
Punishment for attempting to commit offences.
Sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means (false promise of marriage, concealed identity). No IPC counterpart.
Mob lynching: murder by a group of five or more on the ground of race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language or personal belief. No IPC counterpart.
Organised crime. Previously only reachable through state legislation such as MCOCA. No IPC counterpart.
Petty organised crime. No IPC counterpart.
Terrorist act, brought into the general penal code alongside the UAPA. No IPC counterpart.
Snatching, previously charged as ordinary theft. No IPC counterpart.
